payload.text:
Radial-velocity dataset seed300087_diff1.

- 95 observations over a baseline of 485.2 days
- median reported uncertainty: 0.531 m/s
- instruments: instA
- host star mass: 0.787 solar masses
- submission attempts available: 3

Recover the planetary system that produced this signal: the number of
planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Strongly supported simplest hypothesis: 1 planet.

Candidate planet:
- P ≈ 142.71 d

Why this period:
- It is overwhelmingly dominant in the periodogram (power 0.956, FAP ~ 0).
- It is well below the 485 d baseline, so it is constrained by the data.
- The spectral window has no strong feature near 142.7 d, so this is not cadence-driven.
- The other listed peaks are all weak and statistically unconvincing (high FAP), many near daily/cadence aliases or short-period clutter. None are competitive with the 142.7 d signal.
- I do not see a compelling alternative alias in its family: 71.35 d and 285.41 d are the simple half/double relatives, but the periodogram identifies 142.7 d itself as the true dominant peak, and there is no indication the window favors one of those aliases instead.

Plan for the engineer:
- Fit a 1-planet Keplerian at an initial period near 142.7 d.
- After fitting, check residuals; only add another planet if a clear residual signal remains.

HANDOFF: engineer
